tasks.summary: checkpoint.ts (26 new lines, unchanged since c0339f78f) implements saveCheckpoint/checkpointPath exactly to sc2's durability contract: a whole-JSON write to a uuid-suffixed temp file opened exclusively (mode 0o600), fsync'd before the atomic rename, followed by a best-effort directory fsync (tolerating EINVAL/ENOTSUP/EISDIR as "and directory as supported"), with the temp file cleaned up in a finally. Any failure before rename leaves the existing checkpoint at `path` untouched, so a prior valid checkpoint is always retained on persistence failure; rename itself is atomic so pollers never observe a partial document. The coordinator.ts caller (context) awaits save() before each task transition and stops scheduling (without discarding the last durable file) when save() throws, matching the required behavior end-to-end.

testCoverage.explanation: I executed `node --import tsx --test --test-force-exit src/workflow/code-review/task-review/__tests__/coordinator.test.ts` myself in the current checkout; checkpoint.ts is byte-identical between c0339f78f and the current checkout (confirmed via `git diff c0339f78f -- checkpoint.ts`, no output), so this run is valid evidence against the committed implementation even though coordinator.test.ts itself has since gained one additional unrelated test. All 7 tests passed, including the three named tests: 'task review admission...' reads the checkpoint file from disk via fs.readFile+JSON.parse immediately after start() and again after settlement, proving saveCheckpoint produces a parseable whole JSON file both pre- and post-task; 'task execution: checkpoint before next task...' wraps the real saveCheckpoint (not a pure mock) and asserts the prior task's result is durable on disk before the next provider call begins; 'checkpoint write failure stops scheduling...' also wraps the real saveCheckpoint for writes 1-4 and injects a throw on write 5, then asserts only t1's result is retained on disk and no third task runs — this is genuine filesystem-level exercise of the atomic-replace path, not a stub.

limitations: One minor non-blocking edge case noted but not raised as a finding per the optional-improvements rule: if the write/rename path throws AND the outer finally's unlink(temporary) also throws with a non-ENOENT error, the unlink error masks the original persistence error. This doesn't violate any stated requirement (the on-disk checkpoint is still correctly retained either way) and is narrative advice only.
advice: Consider preserving the original error (e.g. via AggregateError or logging-then-rethrow) if the cleanup unlink in the outer finally also fails, so a genuine write failure isn't masked by an unrelated cleanup error. Low priority — behavior and durability guarantees are unaffected either way.
